title: OpenMHS registry triage overrides
description: One file under MHS/registry/overrides/. Each entry fixes the triage decision of one corpus repo and wins over the ordered triage rules (MHS/registry/triage.py). Regeneration reads these files and never writes them. A justification is one line that says why the curated decision is right.

sourcePath.description: Source evidence only: normalized relative POSIX path; spaces allowed; no traversal or control characters. Package paths are unchanged.

family.description: Integration family; required for direct-driver and family-config, informative for bridge-runtime.

partner.description: Early-ecosystem partner whose product the repo drives (appendix D); adds the partner term of the rank formula. Records a product relationship, not an endorsement.

flagship.description: On the curated flagship list (rule 8 never skips it).

entry_symbols.description: Entry symbols confirmed in the clone at the card's commit (a recon proposal that tools/check_recon.py checked and a maintainer accepted). They replace the scan's entry symbols on the card, with confidence override. Only for direct-driver and family-config.

symbol.description: Source-only dotted class or pyfile:path.py#Class / pyfile:path.py#* selector; never a runtime import target.

capability_classes.description: Catalogue capability classes a reviewer confirmed in the clone's source. They replace the scan-derived candidate classes on the card, so the card's risk floor (the highest risk_class of the classes, CAP-017) follows them; build_registry.py refuses a class that is not a stable catalogue class. Only for direct-driver and family-config.

modes.description: The record's complete mode set, a reviewer's reading of the source where the scan's modes are wrong (a real-hardware route recorded as simulated). It replaces the record's modes, so simulation, hardware_free, the device plan and the card's safety.expected_mode follow it; hardware comes first (triage.py checks the order). It never removes a hardware mode the scan found, and build_registry.py refuses it on a record of tier D or X, which has no modes.

served_mode.description: Serve the simulated form of a dual-mode record. The record keeps its modes (hardware first, simulated still present; a modes override still cannot drop hardware) and records x-vendor.classification.served_mode with rule override:served-mode. The card's safety.expected_mode becomes simulated. build_registry.py refuses it unless both modes are present and hardware is first. Only for direct-driver and family-config.

publish_review.description: A reviewer found licence evidence (a licence file and packaging metadata that disagree, or a custom licence the scan read as a standard one) that the owner must decide on before a driver is published: the card says publish_review required whatever its licence class. An override can add this review, never waive one.

omit_sim_contract.description: A reviewer confirmed that the scan's gym registrations, environment classes and MJCF models are not the contract the driver serves (a vendored test scene beside a fake-hardware arm, for example). build_card then leaves models empty, does not take sim_hints, and does not prefer upstream-sim because of that scan. Candidate classes still come from capability_classes when that list is set, and otherwise from the device API. Only for direct-driver and family-config. capability_classes cannot say this: it requires 1 to 8 catalogue ids and does not drop models.

companions.description: Reviewed companion sources (user decision 2026-11-05): corpus repositories cloned locally at their corpus-lock commit that the package's e-stop, its read-back, its declared re-enable and its facts may cite (companion:<alias>/<path>:<LINE>). build_registry.py copies them onto the card with the clone's local_path, repo_url and licence and stops when a package_id is not a corpus record, a commit is not its corpus-lock commit, an alias repeats or a companion is the repository itself. An entry with lock names a clone fetched under work/companions instead (the user's authorisation of 2026-11-05): its commit and profile must be the LOCK.json entry's, its package_id the one that entry's repo_url names, and the card's package must be in that entry's needed_by; build_registry.py copies the LOCK.json path, repo_url, ref and licence. version_evidence ties the package's stack to the companion's: each ref is path:LINE in the tree its side names and must show its token. Only for direct-driver and family-config. One further case (user decision 4, 2026-11-05), and only for a package the user named: hardware_stop true on a lock entry whose profile is not a ROS profile. That package's stop and its fresh read-back may cite it. The hardware backend still needs a human reviewed_by with scope hardware.

lock.description: The work/companions/LOCK.json alias (<owner>__<repo>@<ref>) of a fetched companion clone; absent for a corpus companion.

hardware_stop.description: User decision 4 of 2026-11-05: this lock companion may be cited by that one hardware package's stop and its fresh read-back. Exactly true, and only together with lock. A ROS companion never sets it.

profile.description: A ROS generation-distro-simulator release (ros1-noetic-gazebo11), or, when hardware_stop is true, a non-ROS profile such as micromanager-2.0-gamma-20230120.

ref.description: path:LINE[-END] in the tree its side names
